comparison: Perfect alignment with 100% claim overlap (C4, C63-C70, C110). Both evaluations support the finding that ASPCs from aged mice retain in vitro differentiation capacity, with all reviewers explicitly affirming this as compelling evidence for non-cell-autonomous mechanisms.

Perfect alignment with 100% claim overlap (C136-C137). Both evaluations support the identification of two beige adipocyte subtypes and the potential for therapeutic targeting, though both appropriately frame therapeutic applications as prospective rather than demonstrated.

Strong alignment with 90% claim overlap (C55-C61, C108-C109). Both evaluations support the scRNA-seq characterization of ASPC populations and their gene expression changes. The negative finding regarding ARCs is accepted without challenge by peer reviewers.

Strong alignment with 89.5% claim overlap (C71-C87). Both evaluations support the snRNA-seq identification of four adipocyte populations with distinct molecular signatures. Peer reviewers explicitly highlight the DNL-high white adipocyte cluster as an important contribution to the field.

Strong alignment with 86.7% claim overlap (C31-C44, excluding C29-C30, C41). Both evaluations support the comprehensive evidence for aging-related impairment in beige fat formation. All peer reviewers explicitly affirm this fundamental finding with the data accepted without challenge.

Strong alignment with 60% claim overlap (C5, C70, C113). Both evaluations support the main mechanistic conclusion about non-cell-autonomous effects. Peer reviewers explicitly affirm this interpretation as an important finding for identifying therapeutic approaches.

Strong alignment with 62.5% claim overlap (C97-C105, C107). Both evaluations support the finding that DNL genes are dramatically induced in young mice and suppressed in aged mice. Peer reviewers explicitly highlight this as novel and worth further pursuing, calling it an important contribution.

Strong alignment with 60% claim overlap (C8-C9, C90-C95, C106). Both evaluations support the finding of age-related Npr3 upregulation and its implications for natriuretic peptide signaling. Peer reviewers accept this as supporting a potential therapeutic target.

Moderate alignment with 50% claim overlap (C3, C49-C51). Both evaluations support the lineage tracing evidence for blocked beige adipogenesis in aged mice. All peer reviewers explicitly affirm this finding as novel and compelling, with rigorous methodology.

Partial alignment with 50% claim overlap (C46-C48, C52). OpenEval supports the lineage tracing methodology and notes the low Pdgfra+ contribution as an appropriate caveat. Peer reviewers accept the technical approach but express uncertainty about interpretation, requesting additional quantifications of adipogenic rate and absolute cell numbers.

Minimal overlap (C29-C30 only). OpenEval supports the aging phenotype findings. Peer reviewers raise uncertainty about confounding factors, noting that aging is confounded with body weight and adiposity differences, which limits interpretation of aging as the sole driver.

Minimal alignment with 15.4% claim overlap (C116-C119). OpenEval supports the dormant adipocyte reactivation model as reasonable interpretation. Peer reviewers express uncertainty, questioning whether de novo adipogenesis or reactivation explains early cold response and requesting further discussion of mechanisms.

OpenEval supports claims C1, C10-C28 as established background knowledge appropriately cited from literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as these represent contextual claims rather than novel findings requiring peer assessment.

OpenEval supports claims C111-C112 regarding ARCs being present in immune cells rather than ASPCs, reconciling negative findings with prior literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific clarification.
